title: Punishment for murder
text: Whoever commits murder is punished with death or imprisonment for life and fine. Section 103(2) specifically punishes murder by a group of five or more persons acting together on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language or personal belief (mob lynching).
punishment: Death or life imprisonment, and fine

title: Causing death by negligence
text: Causing the death of any person by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide is punishable. A lower maximum applies to registered medical practitioners during a medical procedure. Section 106(2) provides a harsher punishment for a driver who causes death by rash or negligent driving and escapes without reporting to the police or a Magistrate; check its current enforcement status.
punishment: Up to 5 years and fine (up to 2 years for medical practitioners)

title: Abetment of suicide
text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets (instigates, conspires or intentionally aids) the commission of that suicide is punishable.
punishment: Up to 10 years and fine

title: Dowry death
text: Where a woman dies of burns or bodily injury, or otherwise than under normal circumstances, within seven years of marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives in connection with a demand for dowry, the death is a dowry death and the husband or relative is deemed to have caused it.
punishment: Minimum 7 years, may extend to life imprisonment
keywords: death within seven years of marriage

title: Cruelty to a woman by husband or his relatives
text: A husband or relative of the husband who subjects a woman to cruelty is punishable. Under Section 86, cruelty means wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to her life, limb or health (mental or physical), or harassment to coerce her or her relatives to meet an unlawful demand for property or valuable security such as dowry.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
text: Whoever does any act intending or knowing it is likely to cause bodily pain, disease or infirmity to another person voluntarily causes hurt and is punishable under Section 115(2).
punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
text: Grievous hurt includes fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth, permanent loss of sight or hearing, permanent disfiguration of the head or face, and any hurt which endangers life or causes severe bodily pain for 15 days. Voluntarily causing grievous hurt is punishable under Section 117(2).
punishment: Up to 7 years and fine

title: Acid attack
text: Causing permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming or disfigurement by throwing acid or administering it is punishable; the fine is paid to the victim and must be just and reasonable to meet medical expenses. Attempting to throw acid is separately punishable under Section 124(2). Victims are entitled to free medical treatment in all hospitals.
punishment: Minimum 10 years up to life and fine; attempt 5 to 7 years and fine

title: Wrongful restraint
text: Voluntarily obstructing any person so as to prevent that person from proceeding in any direction in which they have a right to proceed is wrongful restraint.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both

title: Wrongful confinement
text: Wrongfully restraining a person so as to prevent them from proceeding beyond certain limits, for example locking someone in a room or house, is wrongful confinement. Longer confinement attracts higher punishment.
punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both (basic offence)

title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force on any woman, intending or knowing it to be likely that her modesty will be outraged, is punishable. This covers molestation, groping and unwanted physical touching.
punishment: 1 to 5 years and fine

title: Sexual harassment
text: A man commits sexual harassment by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, a demand or request for sexual favours, showing pornography against the will of a woman, or making sexually coloured remarks.
punishment: Up to 3 years or fine or both; up to 1 year for sexually coloured remarks

title: Voyeurism
text: Watching or capturing the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would expect not to be observed, or disseminating such an image, is voyeurism. Consent to capture an image does not imply consent to share it.
punishment: 1 to 3 years and fine on first conviction; 3 to 7 years on subsequent conviction

title: Stalking
text: A man who follows a woman and contacts or attempts to contact her repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest, or monitors her use of the internet, email or any electronic communication, commits stalking.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine on first conviction; up to 5 years on subsequent conviction

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
text: Uttering any word, making any sound or gesture, or exhibiting any object intending that it be heard or seen by a woman to insult her modesty, or intruding upon her privacy, is punishable. This covers eve-teasing and obscene comments.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

title: Rape and its punishment
text: Section 63 defines rape, including sexual acts against a woman's will or without her free consent. Section 64 prescribes punishment, with enhanced punishment for police officers, public servants, relatives, persons in a position of trust and repeat offenders. The victim's identity must not be disclosed, and the victim has the right to free medical treatment and to have her statement recorded by a woman officer.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of at least 10 years, up to life, and fine

title: Sexual intercourse by deceitful means
text: Having sexual intercourse with a woman by deceitful means, or by making a promise to marry her without any intention of fulfilling it, where it does not amount to rape, is punishable. Deceitful means include false promises of employment or promotion, or marrying after suppressing identity.
punishment: Up to 10 years and fine

title: Theft
text: Dishonestly taking any movable property out of the possession of a person without consent is theft. Repeat offenders face a minimum sentence. For a first-time theft of property worth less than Rs. 5,000 where the property is returned, community service may be ordered.
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both; 1 to 5 years and fine on second conviction

title: Snatching
text: Theft is snatching if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly, quickly or forcibly seizes or grabs movable property from a person, such as a chain, phone or bag.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

title: Extortion
text: Intentionally putting a person in fear of injury to themselves or another, and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver property or valuable security, is extortion. Blackmail demanding money under threat of exposing photos or information is covered.
punishment: Up to 7 years, or fine, or both

title: Robbery
text: Theft or extortion becomes robbery when the offender causes or attempts to cause death, hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of these, in committing it.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; up to 14 years on a highway between sunset and sunrise

title: Criminal breach of trust
text: Whoever, being entrusted with property or dominion over it, dishonestly misappropriates it, converts it to their own use, or disposes of it in violation of the trust is guilty of criminal breach of trust. This applies, for example, when someone given money or goods for a purpose keeps it.
punishment: Up to 5 years, or fine, or both

title: Cheating
text: Deceiving any person and fraudulently or dishonestly inducing them to deliver property, or to do or omit anything they would not otherwise do, which causes or is likely to cause damage to them, is cheating. Cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property is punished more severely under Section 318(4).
punishment: Up to 3 years (basic); up to 7 years and fine under Section 318(4)

title: Cheating by personation
text: Cheating by pretending to be some other person, or knowingly substituting one person for another, is cheating by personation. This covers frauds where callers pretend to be bank officials, police or relatives.
punishment: Up to 5 years, or fine, or both

title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
text: Entering property in another's possession with intent to commit an offence, intimidate, insult or annoy, or unlawfully remaining there, is criminal trespass. Doing so in a building used as a dwelling is house-trespass.
punishment: Up to 3 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000 (trespass); up to 1 year or fine up to Rs. 5,000 (house-trespass)

title: Mischief
text: Causing destruction of, or damage to, any property with intent or knowledge that it will cause wrongful loss or damage is mischief. Punishment increases with the value of the loss.
punishment: Up to 6 months or fine (basic); higher for greater loss

title: Forgery
text: Making a false document or electronic record with intent to cause damage, support a false claim, cause a person to part with property, or commit fraud is forgery. Forgery for the purpose of cheating is punished more severely.
punishment: Up to 2 years or fine (basic); up to 7 years and fine for forgery for cheating

title: Criminal intimidation
text: Threatening a person with injury to their person, reputation or property, or to anyone they are interested in, intending to cause alarm or to make them do something they are not legally bound to do, is criminal intimidation. Threats to cause death or grievous hurt carry a higher punishment.
punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both; up to 7 years for threats of death or grievous hurt

title: Intentional insult to provoke breach of peace
text: Intentionally insulting a person in any manner, thereby giving provocation, intending or knowing it is likely to cause them to break the public peace or commit another offence, is punishable.
punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Defamation
text: Making or publishing any imputation concerning a person by words, signs or visible representations, intending to harm or knowing it will harm their reputation, is defamation, subject to exceptions such as truth for the public good and fair comment.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, or community service

title: Kidnapping
text: Taking or enticing a child or a person of unsound mind out of the keeping of their lawful guardian without consent, or conveying a person beyond the limits of India without consent, is kidnapping.
punishment: Up to 7 years and fine

title: Marrying again during lifetime of spouse (bigamy)
text: Whoever, having a living husband or wife, marries again where the second marriage is void because it takes place during the life of the spouse, is punishable. Concealing the former marriage attracts a higher punishment.
punishment: Up to 7 years and fine; up to 10 years if the former marriage was concealed

title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
text: Driving any vehicle or riding on a public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury is punishable.
punishment: Up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both

title: Unlawful compulsory labour
text: Unlawfully compelling any person to labour against their will is punishable.
punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR, Zero FIR, e-FIR)
text: Every information relating to a cognizable offence must be recorded by the officer in charge of a police station, irrespective of the area where the offence was committed (Zero FIR). Information may be given orally or by electronic communication (e-FIR), which must be signed within three days. A copy of the FIR must be given to the informant free of cost. Statements of women victims of certain sexual offences are recorded by a woman officer. For offences punishable with 3 to 7 years, a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days may be conducted.

title: Remedy when police refuse to register FIR
text: Any person aggrieved by the refusal of an officer in charge of a police station to record information may send the substance of the information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police. If satisfied that it discloses a cognizable offence, the SP will investigate personally or direct an investigation. If this also fails, the person may apply to the Magistrate.

title: Magistrate may order police investigation
text: A Magistrate empowered to take cognizance may order the police to investigate a cognizable offence on an application supported by an affidavit, after the applicant has approached the Superintendent of Police under Section 173(4). Alternatively, a private complaint may be filed before the Magistrate under Section 223.

title: Victim to be informed of investigation progress
text: The police must inform the informant or victim of the progress of the investigation within 90 days, by any means including electronic communication. On completion, a police report is filed before the Magistrate.

title: When police may arrest without warrant; notice of appearance
text: Police may arrest without warrant only in specified circumstances and must record reasons. For offences punishable with up to 7 years, where arrest is not necessary, the police must issue a notice of appearance under Section 35(3) instead of arresting. No arrest may be made for an offence punishable with less than 3 years without permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police if the person is infirm or above 60 years of age.

title: Right to know grounds of arrest and right to bail
text: Every person arrested without warrant must be told immediately the full particulars of the offence and the grounds of arrest. A person arrested for a bailable offence must be informed that they are entitled to be released on bail and may arrange sureties.

title: Duty to inform family of arrest
text: The police must immediately inform a relative, friend or nominated person about the arrest and the place where the arrested person is held, and also inform the designated police officer in the district. An entry must be made in a register at the police station.

title: Right to meet an advocate during interrogation
text: A person arrested and interrogated by the police is entitled to meet an advocate of their choice during interrogation, though not throughout the interrogation.

title: Production before Magistrate within 24 hours
text: No person arrested without warrant may be detained in police custody for more than 24 hours, excluding the time needed for the journey, without a special order of a Magistrate.

title: Arrest of women
text: Where a woman is to be arrested, she may be touched only by a female police officer, unless circumstances otherwise require. No woman may be arrested after sunset and before sunrise except in exceptional circumstances, and then only by a woman police officer with the prior permission of the Judicial Magistrate.

title: Medical examination of arrested person
text: An arrested person must be examined by a medical officer soon after arrest, and the injuries or marks of violence must be recorded. The arrested person or their nominee is entitled to a copy of the report.

title: Women, children and elderly need not go to the police station
text: Police may require attendance of witnesses for questioning, but a male under 15 or above 60 years, a woman, or a mentally or physically disabled or acutely ill person cannot be required to attend anywhere other than their place of residence.

title: Bail in bailable offences
text: A person accused of a bailable offence has a right to be released on bail, by the police or by the court. A person unable to furnish surety within a week is presumed indigent and may be released on a personal bond.

title: Bail in non-bailable offences
text: In non-bailable offences, bail is at the discretion of the court, which considers the nature of the accusation, the evidence, and the risk of the accused fleeing or tampering with evidence. Special consideration applies to women, children, and sick or infirm persons.

title: Anticipatory bail
text: A person who has reason to believe they may be arrested for a non-bailable offence may apply to the High Court or Court of Session for a direction that, in the event of arrest, they shall be released on bail.

title: Default bail when investigation is not completed in time
text: If the investigation is not completed and a chargesheet is not filed within 60 days (or 90 days for offences punishable with death, life imprisonment, or at least 10 years), the accused is entitled to be released on bail if they apply and furnish bail.

title: Maintenance of wives, children and parents
text: A Magistrate may order a person with sufficient means who neglects or refuses to maintain their wife (unable to maintain herself), minor children, or parents (unable to maintain themselves) to pay a monthly allowance. There is no upper limit on the amount, and interim maintenance may be ordered during the proceedings.

title: Victim compensation scheme
text: Every State Government must have a scheme to provide funds to compensate victims of crime. The victim or dependants may apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority, even where the offender is not traced or identified. Immediate first aid and medical benefits must be provided free.

title: Who is a consumer
text: A consumer is any person who buys goods or hires or avails of services for consideration, including through online, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing, but not a person who obtains goods for resale or commercial purpose.

title: Consumer rights
text: Consumers have the right to be protected against hazardous goods and services, to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price, to be assured access to goods at competitive prices, to be heard, to seek redressal against unfair or restrictive trade practices, and to consumer awareness.

title: Defect in goods
text: A defect means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods which is required by law, contract, or claimed by the trader.

title: Deficiency in service
text: Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance of a service, including any negligent act or omission, or deliberate withholding of relevant information, which causes loss or injury to the consumer. It covers banks, insurers, airlines, telecom, builders, courier, hospitals and other service providers.

title: Unfair trade practice
text: Unfair trade practices include false or misleading representations about goods or services, misleading advertisements, not issuing a bill or cash memo, refusing to take back defective goods or withdraw deficient services and refund the price within the stipulated period or within 30 days, and disclosing a consumer's personal information without consent.

title: Filing a complaint before the District Commission
text: A complaint about goods sold or services provided may be filed before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission by the consumer, a recognised consumer association, or the Central or State Government. It can be filed electronically through the e-Jagriti (formerly e-Daakhil) portal. A lawyer is not mandatory.

title: Jurisdiction of the District Commission
text: The District Commission hears complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed Rs. 50 lakh (the State Commission hears up to Rs. 2 crore, and the National Commission above that, as revised by the 2021 Rules). A complaint can be filed where the complainant resides or personally works for gain, where the opposite party resides or has a branch, or where the cause of action arose.

title: Admission of complaint within 21 days
text: The District Commission should decide whether to admit a complaint within 21 days of filing; if it does not decide within that period, the complaint is deemed admitted. Complaints should be decided within 3 months, or 5 months if testing of goods is required.

title: Reliefs the Consumer Commission can grant
text: The Commission may order removal of the defect, replacement of goods, refund of the price with interest, compensation for loss or injury including mental agony, punitive damages, discontinuance of unfair trade practices, withdrawal of hazardous goods, and payment of litigation costs.

title: Limitation period for consumer complaints
text: A consumer complaint must be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose. A delay may be condoned if sufficient cause is shown and the Commission records its reasons.

title: Product liability of manufacturer, service provider and seller
text: A manufacturer is liable for harm caused by a product with a manufacturing or design defect, deviation from specifications, breach of express warranty, or inadequate instructions or warnings. Service providers and product sellers (including e-commerce sellers in some cases) are liable on similar grounds.

title: Complaints to the Central Consumer Protection Authority
text: Complaints about violations of consumer rights, unfair trade practices, or false or misleading advertisements that affect consumers as a class may be sent in writing or electronically to the District Collector, the regional office, or the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA).

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Definition of domestic violence
text: Domestic violence includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse (insults, ridicule, name-calling, threats), and economic abuse (depriving the woman of money, stridhan or the shared household), as well as harassment to meet an unlawful dowry demand.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Aggrieved person, domestic relationship and shared household
text: An aggrieved person is any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship (by marriage, a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or as family members living together in a shared household) and alleges domestic violence. A complaint may be made against the husband, male partner, and their relatives, including female relatives.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate for reliefs
text: An aggrieved woman, a Protection Officer, or any other person on her behalf may apply to the Magistrate for one or more reliefs. The first hearing is ordinarily fixed within 3 days of receipt, and the Magistrate should endeavour to dispose of the application within 60 days.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Right to reside in the shared household
text: Every woman in a domestic relationship has the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or interest in it. She cannot be evicted or excluded from it except in accordance with the procedure established by law.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection orders
text: The Magistrate may pass a protection order prohibiting the respondent from committing domestic violence, entering her workplace or school, communicating with her, alienating assets or operating joint bank accounts, or causing violence to her relatives or helpers.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Residence orders
text: The Magistrate may restrain the respondent from dispossessing the woman from the shared household, direct the respondent to remove himself, or direct the respondent to secure alternate accommodation or pay rent for her.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Monetary relief
text: The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief for expenses and losses suffered, including loss of earnings, medical expenses, loss caused by destruction or removal of property, and maintenance for the woman and her children.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Custody orders and compensation
text: The Magistrate may grant temporary custody of children to the aggrieved woman (Section 21) and may direct the respondent to pay compensation and damages for injuries, including mental torture and emotional distress (Section 22).

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Interim and ex parte orders
text: Where the application prima facie discloses domestic violence or its likelihood, the Magistrate may grant interim and even ex parte orders on the woman's affidavit, without waiting for the respondent.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection Officers and their duties
text: Each district has Protection Officers who help the woman prepare a Domestic Incident Report, file an application, obtain free legal aid, and access shelter homes and medical facilities.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Penalty for breach of protection order
text: Breach of a protection order or interim protection order by the respondent is an offence.
punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 20,000, or both

title: Penalty for giving or taking dowry
text: Giving, taking, or abetting the giving or taking of dowry is an offence. Voluntary presents given at the time of marriage without demand, and entered in a list, are not dowry.
punishment: Minimum 5 years and fine of at least Rs. 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more

title: Penalty for demanding dowry
text: Demanding dowry, directly or indirectly, from the parents, relatives or guardian of a bride or bridegroom is punishable.
punishment: 6 months to 2 years and fine up to Rs. 10,000

title: Dowry to be held for the benefit of the wife
text: Any dowry received by a person other than the woman must be transferred to her within three months, and is held in trust for her benefit until then. Failure is punishable.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Sexual harassment at the workplace
text: Sexual harassment includes unwelcome physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature. Implied or explicit promises of preferential treatment, threats about employment, or creating an intimidating or hostile work environment also amount to sexual harassment. The workplace includes any place visited during employment, including transport provided by the employer.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Internal Committee (ICC)
text: Every employer with 10 or more employees must constitute an Internal Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least half its members women and one external member from an NGO or person familiar with sexual harassment issues.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Local Committee
text: Each district has a Local Committee (constituted by the District Officer) to receive complaints from establishments with fewer than 10 employees, where the complaint is against the employer, or from domestic workers and unorganised sector workers.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Complaint of sexual harassment
text: An aggrieved woman may make a written complaint to the Internal or Local Committee within three months of the incident (or the last incident in a series). The Committee may extend this by a further three months for sufficient reasons. Committee members must help her put the complaint in writing if needed.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Inquiry, interim relief and action
text: The Committee must complete its inquiry within 90 days. During the inquiry, it may recommend interim relief such as transfer of the woman or the respondent, or leave of up to three months. If the allegation is proved, it recommends action under the service rules and deduction of compensation from the respondent's salary. The employer must act within 60 days.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Conciliation
text: Before an inquiry, the Committee may take steps to settle the matter through conciliation only at the woman's request. No monetary settlement can be the basis of conciliation.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Employer duties and penalties
text: Employers must provide a safe working environment, display the consequences of sexual harassment and the composition of the Internal Committee, organise awareness programmes, and assist in filing a criminal complaint if the woman wishes. Failure to constitute the Committee or comply with the Act is punishable with a fine, which is doubled on repeat, and may lead to cancellation of licence.
punishment: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; higher penalties and licence cancellation on repetition

title: Right to information
text: All citizens have the right to information held by or under the control of any public authority, including records, documents, emails, file notings, orders, reports and samples.

title: How to file an RTI application
text: A request may be made in writing or electronically to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the public authority, in English, Hindi or the official language of the area, with the prescribed fee (Rs. 10 for central public authorities). The applicant need not give any reason for requesting the information. Applicants below the poverty line are exempt from fees. If the information is held by another authority, the PIO must transfer the application within 5 days.

title: Time limit for reply
text: The PIO must provide the information or reject the request with reasons within 30 days of receipt. Information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be provided within 48 hours. Failure to reply in time is deemed refusal, and information must then be supplied free of charge.

title: Exemptions from disclosure
text: Certain information is exempt, such as that affecting sovereignty and security, cabinet papers, information received in confidence from foreign governments, and personal information with no relation to public interest. Information that cannot be denied to Parliament cannot be denied to a citizen.

title: First and second appeal
text: If no reply is received in 30 days or the reply is unsatisfactory, a first appeal lies within 30 days to the First Appellate Authority (an officer senior to the PIO), who should decide within 30 to 45 days. A second appeal lies within 90 days to the Central or State Information Commission.

title: Penalty on the PIO
text: The Information Commission may impose a penalty on a PIO who refuses an application without reasonable cause, fails to reply in time, or gives false information.
punishment: Rs. 250 per day of delay, up to a total of Rs. 25,000

title: Unauthorised access, hacking and computer-related offences
text: Accessing a computer or network without permission, downloading data, introducing viruses, damaging data or denying access attracts liability to pay compensation (Section 43). When done dishonestly or fraudulently it is an offence (Section 66). This covers hacking of email or social media accounts.
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs. 5 lakh, or both (Section 66)

title: Identity theft
text: Fraudulently or dishonestly making use of another person's electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature (such as OTP, PIN or Aadhaar biometrics) is identity theft.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh

title: Cheating by personation using a computer resource
text: Cheating by personation by means of any communication device or computer resource is punishable. This covers online frauds such as fake customer care numbers, phishing links, KYC update scams, job and investment scams, and fake profiles used to obtain money.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh

title: Violation of privacy
text: Intentionally capturing, publishing or transmitting the image of a private area of any person without consent, in circumstances violating their privacy, is punishable.
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs. 2 lakh, or both

title: Publishing obscene or sexually explicit material online
text: Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form (Section 67), or material containing sexually explicit acts (Section 67A), is punishable. Morphed or intimate images shared online without consent are covered.
punishment: Section 67: up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 5 lakh (first conviction). Section 67A: up to 5 years and fine up to Rs. 10 lakh (first conviction)

title: Child sexual abuse material online
text: Publishing, transmitting, creating, browsing, downloading or promoting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts, or enticing children into online sexual relationships, is punishable.
punishment: Up to 5 years and fine up to Rs. 10 lakh (first conviction)

title: Duties of social media platforms (intermediaries)
text: Platforms must follow due diligence and have a Grievance Officer. Under the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, a platform must remove content that exposes a person's private area or shows them in a sexual act, including morphed images, within 24 hours of a complaint by the person or someone on their behalf.

act: RBI Circular on Customer Protection - Limiting Liability in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions, 2017
title: Zero liability for unauthorised electronic transactions
text: If an unauthorised electronic transaction results from the bank's negligence, or from a third-party breach that the customer reports within 3 working days of receiving the bank's alert, the customer has zero liability. If reported within 4 to 7 working days, liability is capped at a limited amount depending on the account type. The bank must credit the disputed amount (shadow reversal) within 10 working days of notification and resolve the complaint within 90 days. Customers who shared their OTP or PIN may bear the loss until they report it.

title: Banking Ombudsman complaint
text: If a bank, NBFC or payment system operator does not reply within 30 days of a complaint, or the customer is not satisfied with the reply, the customer can complain to the RBI Ombudsman free of cost through cms.rbi.org.in. The Ombudsman can award compensation for the loss, plus an additional amount for harassment and loss of time.

title: Time limit for payment of wages
text: Wages must be paid on time: daily wages at the end of the shift, weekly wages on the last working day of the week, fortnightly wages within 2 days after the fortnight, and monthly wages before the 7th day of the next month. When an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, wages due must be paid within 2 working days. The Code replaced the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.

title: Permissible deductions from wages
text: Only authorised deductions, such as fines, absence from duty, recovery of advances, income tax and provident fund, may be made from wages, and total deductions cannot exceed 50% of the wages.

title: Claims for unpaid wages
text: An employee or trade union may file a claim for unpaid or delayed wages, wages below the minimum, or illegal deductions before the authority appointed under the Code, generally within three years. The authority can order payment with compensation.

title: Equal pay and minimum wages
text: No employer may discriminate on the ground of gender in wages or recruitment for the same or similar work (Section 3). No employer may pay less than the notified minimum wage (Section 5).
old_equivalent: Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 and Minimum Wages Act, 1948

act: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (now Industrial Relations Code, 2020)
title: Retrenchment and wrongful termination of workmen
text: A workman with at least one year of continuous service cannot be retrenched without one month's written notice (or wages in lieu) and retrenchment compensation of 15 days' average pay for every completed year of service. A workman who is discharged, dismissed or retrenched may raise an individual dispute and approach the Labour Court or Tribunal.

act: Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 (now Code on Social Security, 2020)
title: Gratuity
text: An employee who has rendered at least five years of continuous service is entitled to gratuity on retirement, resignation, death or disablement, at 15 days' wages for every completed year, subject to a ceiling of Rs. 20 lakh. The five-year condition does not apply on death or disablement. Gratuity must be paid within 30 days of becoming payable, failing which interest is due.

act: Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (now Code on Social Security, 2020)
title: Maternity leave and protection from dismissal
text: A woman employee is entitled to paid maternity leave of up to 26 weeks for her first two children (12 weeks thereafter). Dismissing or discharging a woman during her maternity absence is prohibited.

title: Abolition of bonded labour
text: The bonded labour system is abolished. Every bonded labourer is freed and discharged from any obligation to render bonded labour, and any bonded debt is extinguished. Compelling a person to render bonded labour is punishable. The District Magistrate is responsible for release and rehabilitation.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine
keywords: forced to work to repay loan

title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficient funds
text: If a cheque issued to discharge a debt or liability is returned unpaid for insufficient funds or exceeding arrangement, the drawer commits an offence, provided the cheque was presented within its validity (3 months), the payee sent a written demand notice within 30 days of receiving the bank's return memo, and the drawer failed to pay within 15 days of receiving the notice.
punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both

title: Filing the cheque bounce complaint
text: The complaint must be filed in writing by the payee within one month after the 15-day notice period expires. It is filed before the court within whose jurisdiction the payee's bank branch (where the cheque was presented) is situated.

title: Interim compensation in cheque bounce cases
text: The trial court may order the drawer to pay interim compensation of up to 20% of the cheque amount to the complainant. In an appeal against conviction, the appellate court may require deposit of at least 20% of the fine or compensation.

title: Cheque bounce offences are compoundable
text: Offences under the Act are compoundable, which means the parties can settle and the case can be closed on payment at any stage, including through Lok Adalat or mediation.

act: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and Limitation Act, 1963
ref: Order XXXVII and Limitation Act Schedule
title: Recovering money lent: legal notice and summary suit
text: Money lent or owed can be recovered through a civil suit. A suit on a written contract, promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque may be filed as a summary suit under Order XXXVII, where the defendant must seek leave to defend. A suit for recovery of money lent is generally to be filed within three years. A legal notice demanding payment is usually sent first.

title: Notice to end a tenancy
text: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a monthly tenancy can be terminated by 15 days' written notice, and a yearly lease of agricultural or manufacturing property by six months' notice. The notice must be in writing, signed, and delivered to the other party. State rent control laws may give tenants further protection.

title: Rights and liabilities of landlord and tenant
text: Subject to the agreement, the landlord must disclose material defects and put the tenant in possession, and the tenant may enjoy the property without interruption so long as rent is paid. The tenant must pay rent on time, keep the property in good condition and restore it at the end of the lease, and must not use it for purposes other than agreed.

title: Suit for recovery of possession after illegal dispossession
text: A person dispossessed of immovable property without consent and otherwise than in due course of law may file a suit to recover possession within six months of dispossession, without having to prove title. A landlord cannot forcibly evict a tenant by changing locks or removing belongings.

act: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (applies where adopted by the State)
title: Security deposit, landlord entry and essential services
text: Where adopted, the Model Tenancy Act caps the security deposit at two months' rent for residential premises, requires the deposit to be refunded when the tenant vacates (after lawful deductions), requires 24 hours' written notice before the landlord enters, and prohibits the landlord from cutting off essential supplies such as water and electricity. Disputes go to a Rent Authority. Check your State's tenancy law.

title: Right to property
text: No person shall be deprived of their property save by authority of law. Although no longer a fundamental right, it is a constitutional right enforceable before the High Court.

title: Daughters' equal right in ancestral (coparcenary) property
text: Since the 2005 amendment, a daughter is a coparcener by birth in a Hindu joint family in the same manner as a son, with the same rights and liabilities in coparcenary property, regardless of whether her father was alive on the date of the amendment.

title: Succession when a Hindu man dies without a will
text: When a Hindu male dies intestate, his property passes first to Class I heirs, including his widow, sons, daughters and mother, who take simultaneously and in equal shares (each widow, son, daughter and the mother taking one share).

title: Duty of driver in case of accident
text: When a person is injured in an accident, the driver must take reasonable steps to secure medical attention, including taking the injured person to the nearest hospital, unless prevented by mob fury or circumstances beyond control, and must inform the nearest police station as soon as possible and in any case within 24 hours.

title: Protection of Good Samaritans
text: A Good Samaritan who in good faith gives emergency medical or non-medical help to an accident victim, or transports them to hospital, is not liable for any civil or criminal action for injury or death of the victim and cannot be compelled to disclose their identity.

title: Compensation for hit-and-run accidents
text: In a hit-and-run accident where the vehicle cannot be traced, the victim can claim fixed compensation from the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund: Rs. 2 lakh for death and Rs. 50,000 for grievous hurt, under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022. The claim is made to the Claims Enquiry Officer (usually the SDM/Tehsildar).

title: Compensation without proof of fault
text: The owner or insurer is liable to pay fixed compensation of Rs. 5 lakh for death and Rs. 2.5 lakh for grievous hurt, without the claimant having to prove wrongful act, neglect or default.

title: Claim before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
text: The injured person, the owner of damaged property, or the legal representatives of a deceased person can file a claim for compensation before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) having jurisdiction where the accident occurred, where the claimant resides or carries on business, or where the defendant resides. The 2019 amendment requires filing within six months of the accident. The police's accident report (DAR) is also treated as a claim application.

title: Cashless treatment of road accident victims
text: Under the Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme framed under Section 162, accident victims are entitled to cashless treatment at designated hospitals up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per victim for up to seven days from the accident.

title: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs
text: Driving with blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml, or under the influence of a drug, is an offence.
punishment: First offence: up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both; repeat: up to 2 years, or fine up to Rs. 15,000, or both

title: Equality before law
text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Arbitrary state action violates Article 14.

title: Prohibition of discrimination
text: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. No citizen may be denied access to shops, restaurants, hotels, wells, tanks, roads and public places on these grounds.

title: Abolition of untouchability
text: Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. Enforcing any disability arising out of untouchability is an offence punishable under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

title: Freedom of speech, assembly, movement and profession
text: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression, to assemble peaceably without arms, to form associations or unions, to move freely and reside anywhere in India, and to practise any profession, trade or business, subject to reasonable restrictions.

title: Protection in respect of conviction
text: No person can be convicted under a law that did not exist when the act was committed, be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once, or be compelled to be a witness against themselves.

title: Right to life and personal liberty
text: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. The Supreme Court has held that this includes the right to live with dignity, privacy, livelihood, health, shelter, a clean environment, speedy trial, free legal aid, and protection from custodial violence.

title: Right to education
text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 reserves 25% of entry-level seats in private unaided schools for children from weaker sections (Section 12(1)(c)), bans capitation fees and screening (Section 13), and prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment (Section 17).

title: Protection against arrest and detention
text: An arrested person must be informed of the grounds of arrest as soon as possible, has the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of their choice, and must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours (excluding travel time).

title: Prohibition of trafficking, forced labour and child labour
text: Traffic in human beings, begar and other forms of forced labour are prohibited (Article 23). Paying less than the minimum wage has been held to be forced labour. No child below 14 years may be employed in any factory, mine or hazardous employment (Article 24).

title: Right to approach the Supreme Court for fundamental rights
text: Every person has the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights. The Court may issue writs of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.

title: Writ jurisdiction of High Courts
text: Every High Court may issue writs to any person or authority, including the government, to enforce fundamental rights and for any other purpose. This is often the remedy against illegal action by government departments, police inaction, or illegal detention.

title: Equal justice and free legal aid
text: The State shall secure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and shall provide free legal aid so that no citizen is denied justice because of economic or other disabilities.

act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens
text: A senior citizen (60 years or above) or parent who cannot maintain themselves from their own earnings or property can claim maintenance from their adult children or grandchildren. A childless senior citizen can claim from relatives who will inherit their property. Maintenance covers food, clothing, residence, medical attendance and treatment.

act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title: Application to the Maintenance Tribunal
text: An application for maintenance is filed before the Maintenance Tribunal (usually headed by the SDM). The Tribunal can grant interim maintenance and should decide within 90 days. No lawyer is needed. The Act fixes a maximum monthly maintenance amount set by the State, subject to the statutory ceiling.

act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title: Transfer of property can be cancelled
text: If a senior citizen transfers property by gift or otherwise on the condition that the transferee will provide basic amenities and physical needs, and the transferee fails to do so, the Tribunal can declare the transfer void.

act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title: Abandonment of senior citizens
text: Leaving a senior citizen anywhere with the intention of wholly abandoning them, by a person who has their care or protection, is punishable.
punishment: Up to 3 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both

title: Grounds for divorce
text: Either spouse may seek divorce on grounds including cruelty, adultery, desertion for at least two years, conversion to another religion, incurable mental disorder, and renunciation of the world. A wife has additional grounds, such as the husband's bigamy.

title: Divorce by mutual consent
text: Spouses who have lived separately for one year or more and agree that they cannot live together may jointly file for divorce. The second motion is ordinarily made after six months, but the court may waive this waiting period.

title: Maintenance during case and permanent alimony
text: Either spouse without sufficient independent income may claim maintenance and litigation expenses while the case is pending (Section 24) and permanent alimony on the final decree (Section 25).

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
title: Instant triple talaq is void and an offence
text: Pronouncement of talaq-e-biddat (instant triple talaq) in any form, spoken, written or electronic, is void and illegal. The married Muslim woman is entitled to subsistence allowance for herself and dependent children, and to custody of her minor children.
punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

title: Inter-faith and civil marriage
text: Any two persons, irrespective of religion, may marry under this Act if the man is 21 and the woman is 18 or older, both are of sound mind, neither has a living spouse, and they are not within prohibited degrees. Notice is given to the Marriage Officer and published for 30 days before solemnisation.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Penetrative sexual assault on a child
text: Penetrative sexual assault on any child (a person below 18 years) is punishable with a minimum sentence. Consent of a child is irrelevant. A higher minimum applies where the child is below 16.
punishment: Minimum 10 years, extendable to life, and fine; minimum 20 years if the child is below 16

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Sexual assault and sexual harassment of a child
text: Touching a child's private parts, or making the child touch, with sexual intent is sexual assault, punishable with 3 to 5 years and fine. Sexual harassment of a child, including sexual remarks, gestures, showing pornography, repeatedly following or watching, and threats to use images, is punishable with up to 3 years and fine.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Mandatory reporting
text: Anyone who knows or apprehends that a sexual offence against a child has been or is likely to be committed must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police. Failure to report is punishable. Reports made in good faith attract no liability.
punishment: Failure to report: up to 6 months, or fine, or both

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Child-friendly procedure and confidentiality
text: The child's statement is recorded at their residence or a place of their choice, preferably by a woman police officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector who is not in uniform. The child's identity must not be disclosed by media, and trials must be child-friendly, in camera, with breaks as needed.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
title: Cruelty to a child
text: Any person having actual charge or control of a child who assaults, abandons, abuses, exposes or wilfully neglects the child in a manner likely to cause unnecessary mental or physical suffering is punishable. Children in need of care and protection can be produced before the Child Welfare Committee.
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh, or both

act: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
title: Prohibition of child labour
text: No child below 14 years may be employed in any occupation or process, except helping the family or family enterprise outside school hours in non-hazardous work, or as an artist. Adolescents (14 to 18) cannot be employed in hazardous occupations.
punishment: 6 months to 2 years, or fine of Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 50,000, or both

title: Child marriage
text: A marriage where the girl is below 18 or the boy is below 21 is voidable at the option of the party who was a child. Performing, conducting, directing or promoting a child marriage is punishable. Child Marriage Prohibition Officers and Magistrates can issue injunctions to stop a child marriage.
punishment: Up to 2 years rigorous imprisonment, or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh, or both

title: Who is entitled to free legal aid
text: Free legal services, including a lawyer, court fees and drafting, are available to members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, victims of trafficking or begar, women and children, persons with disabilities, victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought or earthquake, industrial workmen, persons in custody, and persons whose annual income is below the limit set by the State. An affidavit of income is ordinarily sufficient.

title: Lok Adalat
text: Lok Adalats settle pending or pre-litigation disputes by compromise, including cheque bounce, bank recovery, motor accident, matrimonial (other than divorce), labour and utility bill disputes. The award is deemed a decree of a civil court, is final and binding with no appeal, and court fees paid are refunded.

title: Permanent Lok Adalat for public utility services
text: Permanent Lok Adalats decide disputes about public utility services such as transport, postal, telephone, electricity, water, sanitation, hospitals, insurance and banking. They first try conciliation and may then decide the dispute on merits. Their award is final.

act: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
title: Offences of atrocities
text: Acts by non-SC/ST persons against members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes are punishable as atrocities. These include intentionally insulting or intimidating them with intent to humiliate in any place within public view, using caste names to abuse, wrongful dispossession of land, forcing inedible substances, social or economic boycott, preventing use of public places or water sources, and forced labour.
punishment: 6 months to 5 years and fine for most offences; higher for serious offences

act: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
title: No anticipatory bail and no preliminary enquiry
text: Anticipatory bail is not available to a person accused of an offence under this Act where a prima facie case is made out. No preliminary enquiry is required before registering an FIR, and no approval is needed before arrest.

act: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
title: Rights of victims and Special Courts
text: Victims and witnesses are entitled to protection, to be informed of every court proceeding, to be heard on bail and other matters, to travel and maintenance expenses, and to relief and rehabilitation including monetary relief. Exclusive Special Courts try these offences, and the chargesheet must be filed within 60 days.
